title: Keyboard Manager shortcut remapping is unstable and randomly invalid

status.label: Awaiting the existing scope and recovery clarification
status.detail: A July 18, 2026 follow-up asks whether only application shortcuts fail and whether restarting the target app or PowerToys restores them; no author reply is present.

judgment.rationale: The original report lists PowerToys 0.98.1 and describes global shortcut and key remaps becoming invalid after hours, with restart of the target application reported as a workaround. Multiple users describe related paste-like output or remaps failing after restart, but their configurations and outcomes differ. A July 18, 2026 follow-up already asks whether only application shortcuts fail and which restart restores them; no original-author response is present. Do not duplicate the question or merge distinct reports into one proven root cause.
evidence: The original report gives Win+F1/Win+F2 shortcut mappings and Caps Lock-to-Enter key mapping on PowerToys 0.98.1, Windows 10 21H1, user install, running as administrator.
The reporter says remaps stop working after several hours to a day and restarting the target application can restore them.
Other commenters report paste-like output, failures in Microsoft 365, and remaps needing a toggle after reboot; these are not identical reproduction details.
A July 18, 2026 follow-up asks whether only application shortcuts fail and whether restarting target apps or PowerToys is the workaround; no original-author reply is present.
Diagnostic ZIPs are already attached by multiple reporters.
judgment.recommended_action: Wait for the original reporter to answer the existing scope/recovery question; review the supplied diagnostics before requesting any new evidence.

fix_assessment.rationale: The original report may involve Keyboard Manager shortcut or key-remap state becoming stale after prolonged use, but other commenters describe different paste and restart behaviors. Scope and recovery must be clarified before selecting a common root cause.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep saved remappings active after normal application use
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Keyboard Manager's remap state may become invalid or stop dispatching after extended use, but the reports may represent multiple separate issues, including target-app-specific state and sequence output behavior.
plan: Wait for the original reporter's answer to the existing scope and recovery request.
Use the original diagnostic ZIP to compare the time remaps stop working with the reported target-app restart.
Separate the original Win+F1/Win+F2 and Caps Lock-to-Enter scenario from other users' paste/restart reports.
Trace and correct only the confirmed state-loss path, with regression coverage for persistent remaps.
verification: Verify the original key and shortcut remaps remain active through the reported normal-use interval.
Verify the remaps recover without restarting the target application if Keyboard Manager is at fault.
Verify independent text-sequence/paste reports are not regressed by a state fix.

confidence.rationale: The original report is detailed and multiple users confirm related symptoms, but the conditions and recovery mechanisms differ and the latest scope question is unanswered.

issue_context.summary: The original reporter says saved key and shortcut remaps become inactive after hours of use and may recover when the target application restarts.
known_information: The original report lists PowerToys 0.98.1, Windows 10 21H1, user installation, and running as administrator.
The original mappings are Win+F1 to Ctrl+Alt+W, Win+F2 to Ctrl+Alt+1, and Caps Lock to Enter.
The original reporter says failures appear after several hours to a day and restarting the target application may restore them.
Other commenters report different paste-like and startup/reboot symptoms with existing diagnostics.
The July 18, 2026 follow-up asks whether failures are limited to application shortcuts and which process restart restores them; no original-author reply is present.
inferences: The original report may indicate stale shortcut/remap state, but it is not established that all commenters describe the same defect.
issue_context.analysis: Preserve the current author wait and review existing attachments before requesting new diagnostics. Do not use the similar symptoms as evidence for one broad code change until the original reproduction and recovery path are clarified.
initial_investigation: Read the original report and all five comments, including the separate reports and the latest unanswered follow-up.
No linked fix or exact covering issue was found.

information_gaps.information: Whether only application-specific shortcuts fail and whether restarting the target application or PowerToys restores the original remaps
information_gaps.why_needed: The recovery boundary distinguishes a target-app issue from a Keyboard Manager engine state failure; multiple follow-ups currently describe different symptoms.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply to the existing July 18, 2026 question with whether failures affect only application shortcuts and which process restart restores the original Win+F1/Win+F2 and Caps Lock-to-Enter remaps. The existing diagnostic uploads should be reviewed before collecting more.

actions.note: The existing July 18, 2026 scope and recovery question remains unanswered; diagnostic ZIPs are already attached.

reproduce.title: Reproduce delayed remap failure
prerequisites: Use the original reporter's target application
steps: Verify all three remaps work, then use the target application normally for the reported several-hour interval.
When a remap stops working, record which mapping failed and whether the failure is limited to that application.
Test whether restarting only the target application restores the remaps; then separately test restarting PowerToys if needed.
reproduce.expected_result: The configured remaps remain active during normal use and do not require restarting the target application or PowerToys.
